record.title: GroundedGEO tests evidence-aware ranking against unsupported but relevant-looking text
record.summary: GroundedGEO studies whether generative search rankers can elevate relevant-looking product text without evidence support. In a 50-query e-commerce benchmark, the authors report an unsupported-rich ranking gain on frozen Qwen2.5-7B, with the effect marginal on one other ranker and absent on a third. An oracle-label reranker reduced attack-arm top-three rates in the paper's controlled experiment, but every tested automatic judge failed a preregistered reliability gate and the human-gold arm has unresolved interpretation. The authors do not establish a validated automatic defense or a web-wide effect.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce an evidence-paired benchmark with 50 e-commerce queries and 1,950 cases to test whether generative search rankers reward relevant-looking but unsupported product claims. On a frozen Qwen2.5-7B listwise ranker, unsupported-rich variants gained normalized rank of 0.065–0.092 over clean variants across three claim profiles, with Holm-adjusted significance; the comparable effect was marginal on MiMo-v2.5 and absent on GLM-5.3-Flash.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the paper's frozen pointwise-scoring experiment, a reranker using oracle evidence labels reduced the top-three rate for unsupported-rich candidates from 0.647 to 0.427 and for evidence-laundering candidates from 0.613 to 0.387 at λ=40, with zero measured false suppression on protected arms in that experiment.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: All tested automatic judges failed the paper's preregistered reliability gate. The 370-claim human-gold comparison covered a 10-query holdout and showed adverse collateral whose interpretation the authors mark unresolved. The authors therefore do not validate an automatic defense; the ranking effect is model-dependent and the benchmark is limited to e-commerce queries.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent reproduction of the benchmark and reranking results was not located.
The human-gold arm's divergence from construction and judge labels remains unresolved, and automatic judges failed the preregistered reliability gate.
Transfer to non-e-commerce search, additional rankers and end-to-end retrieval remains unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If the measured failure mode transfers, unsupported but relevant-looking claims could distort generative search and agent choices in consequential workflows. The current consequence is notable rather than major because the experiment covers 50 e-commerce queries, effects vary across three rankers, and automatic evidence matching did not pass the authors' reliability gate.
limitations: The primary rank-promotion effect appears on Qwen2.5-7B, is marginal on MiMo-v2.5 and absent on GLM-5.3-Flash; it is not a universal model result.
The constructed benchmark contains 50 e-commerce queries and does not establish behavior across web search, other domains, adaptive browsing or live products.
All tested automatic judges fail the paper's preregistered reliability gate; oracle labels are not a deployable automatic defense.
The human-gold arm covers a 10-query holdout and its adverse collateral remains unadjudicated in the paper.
The reported results are from one preprint and were not independently reproduced in this review.
brief.summary: GroundedGEO studies whether generative search rankers can elevate relevant-looking product text without evidence support. In a 50-query e-commerce benchmark, the authors report an unsupported-rich ranking gain on frozen Qwen2.5-7B, with the effect marginal on one other ranker and absent on a third. An oracle-label reranker reduced attack-arm top-three rates in the paper's controlled experiment, but every tested automatic judge failed a preregistered reliability gate and the human-gold arm has unresolved interpretation. The authors do not establish a validated automatic defense or a web-wide effect.

technical.claimed_result: On frozen Qwen2.5-7B, unsupported-rich variants achieved +0.065 to +0.092 normalized rank gain over clean candidates across three claim profiles, with Holm-adjusted p-values from 0.035 to 0.0011. On the frozen pointwise scorer, oracle labels reduced unsupported-rich top-three rate 0.647→0.427 and laundering 0.613→0.387 at λ=40; these are author-reported benchmark results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv source establishes the paper and its reported methods/results. It also explicitly reports that all tested automatic judges fail the preregistered reliability gate and that the adverse human-gold arm remains unresolved. the research desk did not reproduce the experiment.
technical.mechanism: GroundedGEO adds a post-hoc claim-level penalty to a candidate's base ranking score when query-relevant claims lack support in a separately supplied evidence packet. The paper tests ranking effects, oracle-label reranking, fixed-text packet twins and evidence-coverage changes.
technical.regime: A constructed benchmark of 50 e-commerce queries, five candidate items per query and 1,950 cases; three frozen listwise rankers for the ranking phenomenon, and a frozen pointwise scorer for the controlled reranking experiment. Human-gold evaluation covers a 10-query holdout.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes its frozen split, tuning rule and implementation. No independent reproduction or end-to-end production evaluation was located in this review.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched clean, supported-rich, neutral-matched, unsupported-rich and evidence-laundering arms; text-only length penalty and oracle evidence labels are among the reported comparators. The paper does not claim superiority over all search-integrity defenses.

brief.title: GroundedGEO tests evidence-aware ranking against unsupported but relevant-looking text
brief.why_it_matters: The study tests a concrete failure mode for systems that choose products or sources by relevance: richer claims can rank well even when the supplied evidence does not support them. Its model-specific results and label-quality failure show why a ranking intervention must be evaluated for both attack suppression and collateral suppression. The findings remain limited to one small e-commerce benchmark and need independent, broader replication.
